Yinyang appendices

How to revise

The author uses this approach to keep Yinyang's central crossed participation and return answerable to actual encounters. Philosophy, personal understanding, and actual work develop through that relation. Revision can begin with a developed idea, changed circumstances, an objection, or an arrangement that no longer fits. Find what has changed, work through its consequences, and let the result correct the understanding that guided the change.

Adapt the approach to your purpose, materials, and environment. You may be writing a different philosophy, revising one personal interpretation, or changing a tool. The connections below help identify what needs attention; their order and extent follow the work. Updating the six personal working files uses the material-refresh sequence below, with retrieval scoped to the affected question. The method itself can also be revised when experience shows a better way to proceed.

Write your own actual revision method

Write the method fitted to your practice at references/situated/revision.md in the private package. This guide explains how to write it; the author's approach below offers adaptable material.

Explain what prompts revision, how relevant philosophy and personal material are obtained, how local scope and connected changes are judged, and how environmental changes reach a checked result. Name usable materials and routes, and the judgments needing your participation. A new philosophy, no website, or different working conditions can change the approach. Let the actual method express these conditions instead of reproducing another author's environment.

Scope and connected changes

Identify the result sought and the part that needs development. Distinguish the revision focus, the material used to judge it, and other parts that need to change. Reading philosophy to assess an interface does not itself select the philosophy for rewriting.

Current focus Corresponding work
Refresh personal Yinyang and its environment Reconsider personal material in light of philosophy and current sources, assess the connected accounts, then inspect the relevant Skills and arrangements.
Revise a philosophical claim or personal interpretation Develop the passage and follow changes in meaning into the accounts, methods, or representations that depend on it.
Repair a Skill, page, tool, or arrangement Diagnose and fix that object. Return to a premise or personal interpretation if the result exposes a mistake there.

Follow substantive changes through their actual dependencies. A wording or presentation correction may finish at its source and reading surface; a changed division of work may also require changing the instructions that implement it. Preserve an explicit stopping boundary and explain any necessary consequence that remains unfinished.

Establish the current material

The private references/personal/ material and the six files under references/situated/ serve different purposes. Personal material retains psychologically relevant experiences, source records, and revisable interpretations. It is the main entrance when the question concerns understanding one's own psychology. The six files condense a personal working model of person–model collaboration: enough direction, personal context, counterpart understanding, relationship, realization, and revision method to make the environment fit the actual person. They do not together constitute a psychological model of that person.

Whenever updating these six working files, refresh their grounds before condensing them again:

  1. Read the person's philosophy. Start with the adopted philosophical expression and relevant developed arguments. Use the current working files to locate what depends on them, without treating an old condensation as a substitute for that philosophy or its supporting material.
  2. Find relevant new references. Check current conversation and available Computer History, dialogue histories, work/version history, or other source records for material bearing on the affected understanding. Follow useful summaries to originals when a consequential claim needs fuller context. Histories have different coverage; observing an action does not reveal its psychological cause. Use actual authorized sources and state material gaps.
  3. Refresh the personal references. Add useful new evidence with its source and context, linking an existing original rather than copying it unnecessarily. Compare it and the philosophy with the maintained interpretations in personal; correct, qualify, reorganize, or retire inaccurate and outdated parts. Preserve attributable originals and meaningful uncertainty. A new reference is not merely another appended trait.
  4. Condense the refreshed material with the philosophy. Revise the affected six-file content and check its connections with the other working files. Select what changes collaboration or environmental design, retaining a route back to the richer personal material. The account should explain what a counterpart needs to understand and do, not attempt a complete psychological portrait. Carry necessary changes into the environment and check their use.

This sequence is a dependency of working-model revision, not a demand to collect new personal facts on every occasion or rewrite all six files each time. A bounded correction may use the current exchange as its new source; inspect relevant histories rather than surveying a whole life. If no new relevant material is found, retain that result honestly. The person contributes experience and judgments unavailable in the inspected sources, while the model carries retrieval, reference maintenance, and condensation. Later feedback can return the work to any earlier interpretation.

Write for the actual use

State relevant objects, relations, evidence, conditions, responsibilities, and consequences in clear language. Distinguish a reported experience, an interpretation, a chosen commitment, and an operational requirement where they would lead to different judgments or actions. Personal information supplies contextual evidence; its presence in an account does not make it a command.

Use direct expression. A philosophical distinction or literary image can clarify a relation; explain its meaning where that relation should guide work. Preserve original expression as attributable material while making the maintained interpretation and practical consequences explicit. Keep extended philosophical arguments at their own source and link them where useful.

Sources and evidence

Choose personal writing, conversation, memory, observed work, and philosophical material because they bear on the question. Retain source identity, time, relevant passages, and enough context to assess consequential claims. Where a summary mediates access to an original, make that relation visible: its selection and omissions can shape an interpretation.

Different materials support different claims. A person's report grounds what they expressed or experienced in context; an explanation offered with it still needs assessment. Observed work shows what happened under inspected conditions. A chosen commitment states a direction; philosophy contributes concepts and reasons. In a fictional reading example, reporting greater ease supports experienced ease, and reaching the right passage supports access. Lasting learning and the cause of improvement need further evidence.

Keep temporal scope and uncertainty intelligible. Later speech may correct an interpretation, describe a new situation, or introduce unresolved conflict. Explain important inferences: what supports them, why the connection matters, and what limits their use. Several summaries of one source add no independent support.

Keep extended episodes and unique originals with their existing owners; give derived accounts usable locators and grounds. In the author's package, the private source entrance is references/personal/sources.md; the package guide explains its placement. Preserve useful originals while retiring redundant summaries. Access for revision does not authorize unrelated personal collection or public disclosure of private quotations, portraits, or unpublished work.

Condensation and reopening

Condensation makes relevant understanding usable in the next collaboration. Retain relations that change interpretation, response, or revision: what an expression answers, its applicability conditions, who reported experience and who proposed an explanation, and a material counterexample or alternative. Write these as coherent prose with sources where needed, without requiring the same fields for every item. Carry original words into a working account when their wording bears meaning; complete originals remain with their source.

Develop accounts from reported experience, observable interaction, and actual results while keeping model interpretations recognizable. Repeated citation of a summary adds no independent evidence. Distinguish a narrated pattern, a chosen collaborative direction, and a verified causal explanation. Do not invent internal psychological states to complete a portrait or apply simulated-persona state scores to actual people. These distinctions can coexist in one natural-language model without splitting it into disconnected archives.

When new material arrives, determine whether it corrects a reading, reflects changed conditions, or introduces an unresolved difference. Qualify, withdraw, or reorganize the relevant account rather than only appending traits; retain the original event and the time its interpretation formed. Check rewritten understanding against currently relevant sources so repeated summarization does not turn inference into fact. Recurring words can provide retrieval entrances; frequency alone does not determine their relational meaning. Newer expression does not override all older material merely by being later.

At useful maintenance points, examine whether the next counterpart can still recover applicability, actual purpose, material open questions, and a path to the grounds. Restore omissions that change those judgments; details irrelevant to current use can remain at their source. A model response and its acceptance, rejection, or modification may themselves become later material, but do not automatically prove the model's prior interpretation. The argument is developed in Condensing revisable relations.

Let the return alter its organizing account

Distinguish what happened to the work from what happened to participation. A corrected paragraph establishes a textual change. A person returning to scrutiny while retaining open generation, or model generation reorganized by the conditions exposed in scrutiny, gives the role-return account its particular content. Describe what is chosen, what was observed, and what remains uncertain. The evidence-refresh sequence above supports this judgment; it is not a fixed sequence that every exchange must perform.

Yinyang's corrective feedback adds a question to revision: can a source, objection, or use result actually change the understanding that receives it? Recasting every contrary case as confirmation would preserve the original account at the cost of its corrigibility. Locate the premise, scope, relation, or realization that the new material bears on, and carry the supported change there. The relevant aim can also need revision; correction is not always restoration of the previous arrangement.

Keep interpretation of a philosopher, personal expression through borrowed concepts, and an independently developed argument distinguishable. An unsupported attribution needs correction; a useful new construction can remain as the author's own contribution with its own reasons. This lets sources retain the power to disagree without treating every creative transformation as a mistake.

When revising a chosen role exchange, check each affected object's meaning: why it is valued, how the person participates, what the counterpart contributes, how their relation changes, what enables it, and how the account is corrected. Those are connected responsibilities, not six copies of one paragraph. Integrate feedback only where it changes a contribution. A rewritten account establishes an authored revision; its effects and developmental claims remain open to use.

Let philosophy revise personal support material

Bring developed philosophy into contact with existing personal material. Which interpretations does it clarify? Which distinctions were missing? Which summaries now mislead? Rewrite derived material so experience, interpretation, chosen direction, and uncertainty remain intelligible. Philosophy helps formulate understanding; attributable expression and actual use ground its personal application.

When a public argument is already maintained elsewhere, link it and retain the private meaning and evidence that this account needs. This keeps the support useful as the philosophy changes.

Let philosophy and personal material revise working accounts

Read the philosophy alongside the personal references refreshed through the sequence above. The six files are working models serving a fitting personal environment, with psychological understanding among their grounds. In the author's Yinyang, orientation articulates adopted values and direction; person grounds understanding of the actual person; counterpart relates available capacity to wanted contribution; relationship explains joint activity; environment explains its realization. The writing guides develop these different responsibilities.

Preserve supported substance and rewrite the relations that changed. Distinguish preference from explanatory hypothesis, wanted role from demonstrated capability, and selected arrangement from observed effect. Read neighboring accounts together so the revision remains coherent. Either participant can generate, object, reason, and revise.

Reconsider the actual revision method too. If it repeatedly creates unnecessary work, obscures a judgment, or fails to carry a change into use, revise the relevant guidance and check whether the new approach helps. Another person's practice can call for different objects, organization, or methods.

Let the model maintain the accounts and check cooperation

The six accounts are working context for the model. The model reads them together, checks the grounds of their claims, and maintains the implications for its contribution and the personal environment. The person need not read these descriptions of themselves or undertake psychological self-analysis to receive useful cooperation.

Assess the accounts through the cooperation they support: does the counterpart understand the request, carry the appropriate work, incorporate correction, and help realize a fitting environment? The person can respond to an actual result or explain a mismatch without first auditing a portrait. A useful workflow change can establish better fit without validating a psychological explanation.

For personal psychological understanding, the entrance is the private personal material. The person may read it, or ask a language model to read and help understand it. This is not an assignment to analyze their own fantasy, reverse their psychological position, or repeatedly evaluate themselves through the six working files. The separate Psychology guide addresses materials, questionnaires, statistics, and practical support.

Philosophy can clarify the concepts and values organizing cooperation. The embodied philosophy essay develops that contribution without prescribing a psychological exercise. Keep reported experience, model interpretation, and observed environmental change distinguishable. Document revisions and environmental changes establish their respective results, not changes in psychological states or mechanisms.

Let the whole Yinyang revise Skills and the environment

Use the connected philosophy and personal understanding to assess the Skills and arrangements relevant to the intended result. Do their purposes, instructions, examples, resources, and actual behavior support the contribution wanted? Include prompts, tools, and interfaces where their dependencies affect it. Specialist Skills retain their own methods and task responsibilities.

Repair actual mismatches: contradictory instructions, inaccessible context, an unsuitable interface, or machinery whose contribution has disappeared. Remove displaced guidance and keep what still works. The environment writing guide develops realization; use your environment's actual authoring, implementation, and publication routes.

Create a usable whole and iterate in view

When creating or revising a work, quickly produce a first usable whole through which the person can encounter the intended result. Let that encounter expose what needs development. Choose the scope around a coherent use, and improve the work from actual use and the person's feedback rather than delaying that encounter to polish isolated details.

Keep human-facing presentation focused, especially on new pages. Include explanations and cautions when they materially change the person's current understanding or action; place supporting detail where it can be consulted without crowding the main view. Avoid dense small-print defensive prose. Omit decorative diagonal external-link arrows (↗); retain arrows that express an actual relationship in a diagram.

For interfaces, prioritize the complete user path and its visible behavior: can the person reach the result, understand the controls, and use them? Check the rendered interface and the consequential end-to-end interactions. Choose additional checks for concrete uncertainty and consequences of failure; a unit test can help isolate a real problem. Keep meaningful checks for high-consequence effects, while deferring unrelated tests and refinements that delay a usable first release without resolving a material risk.

Make progress visible during the work. Show readable screenshots or rendered images of the actual evolving interface in the conversation, including changed diagrams, and explain consequential changes. For a new or substantially changed page, show the actual unpublished version before publication; update the preview after a further material edit. A description of implementation alone does not let the person see or judge the result.

Promptly publish authorized webpage and content changes once the usable version and its necessary checks are ready, so the person can encounter the actual surface. Continue publication without waiting for a response to the preview; incorporate feedback as it arrives and iterate from the published result. Personal authentication, consent, safety, and explicit stopping boundaries keep their scope. Other works can offer an equivalent encounter through a readable draft or a usable artifact, with sharing governed by its actual authorization.

Follow the result back into understanding

Compare a summary with its evidence, a generated copy with its source, and a completion claim with the result reached through the actual entrypoint. An unavailable account calls for delivery repair; an account faithfully followed but producing an unsuitable contribution calls for examining its meaning or the selected relationship.

Carry authorized changes through the affected sources and consumers, then read back what is available to the intended reader or working model. Where copies depend on an authored source, update them through their actual route. Keep private material within its authorized audience.

Compare the intended result with the observable outcome and explain required differences still open. Return to personal material, working accounts, or philosophy when evidence challenges them. Useful output, collaborative fit, and personal development have different grounds; let the claim match what the revision and subsequent use actually establish.
